headline.en: Start with Hangul. Write your way to everyday Korean.

lead.en: A beginner workbook built from our most-used free worksheets. Every unit has a short explanation, tables to copy by hand, practice, and an answer key at the back.

d.en: Consonants, vowels and final consonants (받침) come before everything else.

d.en: Tables to copy, short practice sets and review tests.

d.en: Greetings, numbers and dates, family, food, shopping and the basic particles.
d.ko: 인사 · 숫자와 날짜 · 가족 · 음식 · 쇼핑 · 기초 조사

t.en: Answer key and free online practice

d.en: Mark your own work with the key at the back; QR codes open free practice on everykoreans.com.

problem.q: Reading about Hangul is not the same as writing it.
problem.a: Writing each letter, then each word, is what makes the script automatic. Every unit gives you tables to copy and practice sets to fill in.

steps.d: A short explanation and the tables you need.
Copy the tables, then do the practice.
Mini tests and an answer key to mark your own work.

first-steps-workbook.pick: you are starting from zero or have just learned Hangul

problem.q: Particles are tiny, and they change the whole sentence.

problem.a: The two fill-in questions look easy. The trick is matching the style of the passage exactly. This book teaches each text type first, then drills it.
